subject: FintechCo — Post-demo: API auth, key management & integration next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo — Post-demo: API auth, key management & integration next steps

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap:
- Main asks: server-to-server API auth, key rotation policy, per-environment key isolation, and guidance for embeddings/reranker calls.
- Integration focus: SDK setup, routing for low-latency inference across environments, structured output/tool-calling for our transaction enrichment flow.

What Redwood supports (high level):
- API auth: API keys (long-lived) for quick POC; service accounts + short-lived JWTs (recommended) for production server-to-server flows; OAuth 2.0 for user-delegated flows.
- Key rotation: built-in rotation hooks for service accounts (short-lived tokens) and tooling to rotate API keys programmatically; audit logs for key creation/rotation available in Console.
- Embeddings/reranker: embeddings calls should be made from server-side to protect keys and PII. We support vector store integrations and a reranker pipeline (we can share reference configs).

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive (60m) with your infra/SE and our Solutions Engineer (Dev Patel) to walk SDK auth flows, sample code, and routing options.
2) Share your auth requirements (SSO/SAML certs, service account needs) and any procurement/security questionnaire items — we'll map to our artifacts.
3) We'll provide a short integration guide and a sample key-rotation policy draft.

I attached a short integration guide and an architecture sketch that maps recommended auth patterns to Redwood deployment modes.

If you're good, I'll loop in Dev and Rishi and propose a few times.

Best,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0133

Attachments: redwood-integration-guide.pdf, fintechco-authn-arch.png

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifying questions before we lock in the deep-dive: 

1) Per-environment keys: can we have separate keys per environment (dev/stage/prod) with RBAC so that only specific CI/CD pipelines can create/rotate keys?
2) Rotation: does Redwood enforce rotation for API keys or only provide tools/hooks? We're evaluating automated rotation that integrates with our KMS.
3) Embeddings auth: you mentioned always server-side — does Redwood support temporary tokens for client SDKs to call embeddings indirectly (e.g., proxying) or do you recommend only server-side ingestion?
4) Audit logs: can we get exportable audit logs for key usage (who called which key, from which IP) for SOC/compliance review?

Also attaching our initial security questionnaire (short) — would be great if Rishi or Dev can flag anything that will require longer lead times.

Thanks — Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: FintechCo — Post-demo: API auth, key management & integration next steps

Alex — great questions. Short answers up front, then details and proposed artifacts to share before the deep-dive.

Short answers:
- Per-environment keys & RBAC: Yes. You can create isolated API keys/service accounts per environment. We recommend service accounts with least-privilege roles assigned (Console IAM) and scoped keys for CI/CD.
- Rotation: Redwood provides both programmatic rotation endpoints and CI/CD-friendly hooks; for production we recommend short-lived JWTs minted by your KMS (or Redwood-managed optional KMS). Long-lived API keys can be rotated automatically via our API but rotation enforcement is customer-configurable.
- Embeddings auth: We strongly recommend server-side only for embeddings and reranking. For any client-initiated UX (e.g., embeddings-based suggestions), create a server-side proxy that mints short-lived tokens for the client if you must expose limited functionality.
- Audit logs: Yes — exportable, queryable audit logs with request metadata (key id, timestamp, source IP, model used). We can provide a SOC-friendly export format.

Details & artifacts we can share (attached / linked):
- redwood-integration-guide.pdf: step-by-step SDK + example code for Node/Python including service account flow and sample token minting snippet.
- fintechco-authn-arch.png: recommended architecture diagram mapping service account -> KMS -> token minting -> Redwood runtime.
- redwood-api-key-rotation.md: sample policy with automation snippets (Terraform + CI job hooks) and recommended rotation cadence (30d rolling for sensitive workloads, 90d for less sensitive).
- Security questionnaire mapping: we will annotate your attached questionnaire and return a marked-up copy before the deep-dive.

Proposed next steps (concrete):
1) Schedule the 60m technical deep-dive — please pick a slot here: https://calendly.com/redwood-se/60min (I'll propose a few times as well). Attendees: your infra lead, Priya (security), Dev Patel (SE), Rishi (AE).
2) Share your SSO/SAML metadata and the short security questionnaire you attached — we'll annotate and flag any evidence items we'll need (e.g., SOC 2 report, key rotation logs).
3) We'll send a short Mutual Action Plan doc (1 page) after the call with owners and dates.

Blocking/risks to call out now:
- If you require a customer-managed KMS integration, provisioning has a lead time (we'll include steps in the MAP).
- Any plan to call embeddings directly from mobile clients will require a proxy pattern and short-lived token flow — we can provide a reference implementation.

I attached the artifacts above and linked a HubSpot deal + Confluence page with the SOC artifacts we usually share. Dev/Rishi — can you confirm availability for a deep-dive tomorrow/Wednesday morning?

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
